subject: Subject-level uncertainty for model fit for all gng parameters

messages.author: 4a1b8029ecdd5a87
messages.subject: Subject-level uncertainty for model fit for all gng parameters
parts:
Hello,

Thank you so much for the amazing package and for making it available on python as well now!!

We are running the Go/NoGo modelling and were wondering how to extract subject-level uncertainity for the model fit for each of the parameters in order to use that information as a covariate in our group comparisons. Would it be appropriate to use the information about  se_mean and sd found by typing output_model_gng1[ ["fit" ]] ? (full path is output_model_gng1--> parVals --> fit, which is a S4 [ 1000x4x195] rstan::st S4 object of class stanfit)


Thank you for your help!

Best,
Marcella

messages.author: 47d1400f432367d7
messages.subject: Re: Subject-level uncertainty for model fit for all gng parameters
parts:
Hi Marcella,

Happy to hear you are finding it useful!

Yes, to extract the full posterior distributions you need to use the `fit` object. You can use rstan's built in helper functions to extract parameters from the for object. For example, the following:

pars <- rstan::extract(stanfit_object)

will extract everything into `pars`, which you can then access all the model parameters from. You may find this documentation useful: https://mc-stan.org/rstan/reference/stanfit-method-extract.html

Best,
Nate
